note: Each card's number comes from the artifact behind the page it summarises.

facts.title: Four of the city's five treatment plants run on Pench water
facts.unit: MLD of NMC's 786 MLD treatment capacity is in the four Pench plants (NMC, 2023-24)
facts.interpretation: NMC's Environment Status Report lists five plants: Pench I to IV (136, 175, 120, 115 MLD) and Kanhan (240 MLD). The Pench water is released from Totladoh, the Pench hydro-electric reservoir shared with Madhya Pradesh, into the Navegaon Khairi pick-up dam, and goes to the Mahadula pumping station, at km 48.5 of the old canal route (ESR 2017-18 draft); NMC told the state regulator that a closed pipeline replaced the canal in April 2015. The Kanhan plant draws from the river.
facts.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, s.6.2.1, printed pp.132-133

facts.title: Every taluka in the district reads Safe on its total, the city's own unit included
facts.unit: talukas of Nagpur district assessed Safe in 2025-2026, including the city's own unit, Nagpur (Urban)
facts.interpretation: IN-GRES puts the district at 45.3% of its extractable groundwater drawn in 2025-2026, Safe. Nagpur (Urban), assessed as its own unit from 2023-2024, is Safe in all 3 of its editions. Its 2025-2026 figure of 54.62% is computed with 206 ha of the unit entered as canal command area (16,081 ha the year before), so it is in effect the stage of the non-command part alone; the category, Safe in all three editions, is the steadier comparison. Inside Hingna, the canal command area reads Semi Critical (87.64%).
facts.source_label: IN-GRES dynamic groundwater assessment, 2025-2026

facts.title: Dated promises on the city's water, each on its own document
facts.unit: commitments tracked: 4 delivered, 1 on track
facts.interpretation: Each promise sits on a Government Resolution, a court or tribunal order, an NMC budget or report, the AMRUT 2.0 portal or a funder's document, and each change of status cites a dated document. One has a date moved by NMC that has not yet come; 3 are past their date with no delivery on record, one of them after NMC moved it. 1 is recorded as stalled, and for 12 the promise can be cited but not yet its current status.
facts.source_label: Government Resolutions, court orders, NMC budgets and reports, AMRUT 2.0 (see /nagpur/commitments)

facts.title: Oxygen in the Nag falls on its way through the city
facts.unit: mg/L dissolved oxygen at the Nag's last sampling point in the city, against 3.67 where it leaves Ambazari lake (monsoon 2023)
facts.interpretation: NMC sampled 23 points on the Nag, the Pili and the Pora in the monsoon of 2023. At the last point on each river dissolved oxygen was 0.48 mg/L (Nag), 1.18 (Pili, where it meets the Nag) and 0.81 (Pora). CPCB's bathing-water criterion is 5 mg/L or more.
facts.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Tables 6.13 to 6.16, printed pp.161-166

facts.title: Fewer tankers serving areas the network does not reach
facts.unit: tankers in NMC's 2026-27 budget (published May 2026), against 346 in its earlier count
facts.interpretation: NMC's own count: 346 (dated 2016 in its environment reports and 2018 in its budgets), 193 in 2023, 78 in 2024, 59 in early 2025, 37 in early 2026. The documents do not say whether the count is of vehicles or daily trips.
facts.source_label: NMC Budget 2026-27, Commissioner's speech, p.B-4

facts.title: Water lost between source and consumer
facts.unit: % lost in 2023-24, by NMC's own figures: 706 MLD supplied, 410 MLD billed
facts.interpretation: The report prints 41.91%; 410 of 706 gives 41.93%. The 2022-23 report stated 47%, and its own table's figures give 45% on our arithmetic.
facts.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, s.6.2.1 and Table 6.2, printed p.133

facts.title: NMC's share of the Pench
facts.unit: million cubic metres a year in the State's 2020 plan, rising to 341 after the Lohghogari tunnel
facts.interpretation: The 2020 resolution sets NMC's share at 190 Mcum a year. A WRD engineer described that 190 to the regulator in 2017 as the project plan's 112 plus the 78 sanctioned in 1998; NMC described it as 15% of the complex's 1,262 Mcum. The state water regulator held in 2018 that the 78 is 'legal and intact as on today'. The latest published figures for what the city drew from the Pench are in NMC's draft 2017-18 report (its table is headed 'present' and gives no year), and they disagree: 143 million cubic metres billed, while the four Pench plants treated about 166.
facts.source_label: WRD resolution of 19 Mar 2020 (table on p.2); MWRRA Order 13/2018

facts.title: Totladoh on the day of this snapshot
facts.unit: % of designed live storage on 16 October 2026; Navegaon Khairi 70.7%
facts.interpretation: The state Water Resources Department's daily bulletin. On the same date a year earlier Totladoh held 99.6% and Navegaon Khairi 82.6%. Totladoh is shared with Madhya Pradesh and NMC holds a yearly reservation in it, so the figure is the whole dam's storage, not the city's. The dashboard's reservoir cards carry the daily series.
facts.source_label: Maharashtra WRD Pravah daily dam bulletin

facts.title: Areas that get water for less than two hours a day
facts.unit: command areas with some areas counted as 'dark zones' in 2023-24, against 39 in 2022-23
facts.interpretation: NMC's report counts 'certain areas' in these command areas as dark zones, 'since the water supply was found to be less than 2 h per day'. The reports give no citywide hours of supply.
facts.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, printed p.134

facts.title: Tap-water samples found fit
facts.unit: % of 16,364 samples tested in 2023-24 were fit; 314 were not
facts.interpretation: Tested at the Regional Public Health Laboratory, Nagpur, as NMC reports it.
facts.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, printed p.134

facts.title: The highest stage of groundwater extraction in the district
facts.unit: % of extractable groundwater drawn in Saoner, the highest of 14 talukas (2025-2026)
facts.interpretation: CGWB's Safe class ends at 70%. Katol read Semi Critical in 2019-2020, 2021-2022 and 2022-2023, and Safe since; its 2025-2026 figure of 47.61% follows a larger estimate of what can be drawn, with extraction close to flat.
facts.source_label: IN-GRES dynamic groundwater assessment, 2025-2026

facts.title: Groundwater telemetry under the city
facts.unit: of 101 telemetry wells in the district stand in the city's own unit
facts.interpretation: All 3 are Central Ground Water Board piezometers (Bokhara_1, IMD Nagpur_1, Nara_3), read every six hours on the National Water Data Portal and shown as monthly means; the latest month is June 2026. India-WRIS lists these piezometers as semi-confined, deeper than an ordinary dug well, so the page shows the wells themselves rather than one city water-table depth.
facts.source_label: National Water Data Portal, groundwater telemetry

facts.title: The Kanhan below the city
facts.unit: mg/L highest BOD in 2024 at Agargaon, downstream of Nagpur, against 3.5 at Sinora upstream
facts.interpretation: MPCB samples the Kanhan every month; BOD measures organic pollution, and CPCB's bathing-water criterion is 3 mg/L or less. MPCB recorded the river at Agargaon as dry in June of every year from 2019 to 2024.
facts.source_label: MPCB monthly river readings, Kanhan, 2017-2024

facts.title: Three rivers in CPCB's polluted-stretch list
facts.unit: for the Kanhan, the Kolar and the Wainganga in CPCB's 2025 report
facts.interpretation: Priority I is CPCB's most severe class and Priority V its least. In the earlier editions: the Kanhan II in 2022 and III in 2018; the Kolar V in 2022 and III in 2018; the Wainganga III in 2022 and II in 2018. The Nag, the Pili and the Pora have no CPCB readings, so they are not assessed: MPCB lists five national-programme stations on the Nag and the Pili, but CPCB's river tables up to 2024 carry none of them, and neither list has a station on the Pora.
facts.source_label: CPCB Polluted River Stretches, 2018, 2022 and 2025

facts.title: Sewage treatment against sewage generated
facts.unit: MLD of treatment capacity in 12 operating plants, against an estimated 520 MLD of sewage (73% of supply)
facts.interpretation: NMC's plant table for 2023-24. The sewage figure is the report's estimate, about 73% of the water supplied, and the report asks NMC to measure the real quantity. A further 20 MLD plant at Narsala was on trial run.
facts.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, s.6.2.2 and Table 6.3, printed pp.136-137

facts.title: Water bodies on the map
facts.unit: water bodies in and around the city from the State's 2017-18 survey; 29 of them inside the city's wards
facts.interpretation: MRSAC mapped the district's water bodies at 1:10,000 in 2017-18. The map's frame reaches the Pench reservoirs north of the city, so most are outside it: 731 farm ponds, 547 tanks and 24 reservoirs among them. Names come from MRSAC and, where it gives none, from OpenStreetMap.
facts.source_label: MRSAC water bodies, 1:10,000, 2017-18

facts.title: When two of the city's lakes were built
facts.unit: the year Futala lake was built, as the Supreme Court records; Gorewada followed in 1911
facts.interpretation: The Supreme Court records that Futala was built in 1799 by Gyanoji Bhosale 'to cater to the irrigational needs'; a Nagpur Museum record quoted in the judgment ties it to the Bhonsles' garden at Telankhedi. Gorewada, dammed on the Pili, was built as the city's second source after Ambazari's supply 'was inadequate to meet the demand' (1966 District Gazetteer); the Central Water Commission's register of large dams gives its completion as 1911.
facts.source_label: Supreme Court of India, 2025 INSC 1199, paras 5.3 and 5.3.4; Maharashtra District Gazetteer (1966); CWC National Register of Large Dams (2019)

facts.title: Official flood-line maps for the rivers around the city
facts.unit: register entries of red- and blue-line maps for five rivers and a nalla around the city; none for the Pili
facts.interpretation: The Water Resources Department's legal flood boundaries: the blue line is the 25-year flood and the red line the 100-year flood. The count is of the register's entries for the Nag, the Pora, the Kanhan, the Kolar, the Vena and the Bagdor nalla around the city; the register also lists Nagpur-district entries for the Wainganga, the Jam and the Nand. On the Nag the maps cover a stretch at the city's eastern edge, not its course through the centre. They are scanned maps, so they are linked, not drawn on a map.
facts.source_label: WRD Maharashtra, Flood Line Maps register

facts.title: The network the water travels through
facts.unit: km of distribution mains, 106 water tanks and 4.50 lakh connections
facts.interpretation: NMC's 2026-27 budget (published May 2026). The city is divided into 10 water distribution zones.
facts.source_label: NMC Budget 2026-27, Commissioner's speech, p.B-3

facts.title: 38 wards, 151 councillors
facts.unit: people across 38 wards, as printed in the final ward notification of 4 Oct 2025
facts.interpretation: Ward populations run from 47,216 to 71,187. The notification does not name the census year its figures come from. The ward outlines are MRSAC's map, whose ward populations follow the August 2025 draft; for 7 wards, part of an edge may not follow the final line.
facts.source_label: Final ward notification No. 1600-E.D.-NMC-2025; MRSAC ward layer

facts.title: A normal year's rain
facts.unit: mm a year, IMD gridded data at 21.0 N 79.0 E (1970-2020 mean)
facts.interpretation: IMD's own Nagpur observatory normal is 1,151.2 mm (1991-2020). On this grid cell, June to September bring 87% of a normal year's rain; the wettest year in the record is 1994, at 1,744.2 mm.
facts.source_label: India Meteorological Department, gridded rainfall

facts.title: How much water each source supplies
facts.unit: no per-source supply figure found after NMC's draft 2017-18 report
facts.interpretation: NMC's reports give treatment capacity plant by plant, and its 2023-24 water balance one citywide total, 257.642 million cubic metres of treated water. The latest figures by source are the raw-water bills in NMC's draft 2017-18 report, whose table is headed 'present' and gives no year; they disagree with the treated output the same report gives for each plant.
facts.source_label: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Table 6.2
